Leave-one-source-out range of an aggregated index

Source: R/trend_index.R
index_jackknife.Rd

Recomputes the aggregated index of aggregate_index() leaving out one source at a time and reports the range of the results and the source whose removal moves the index most.

Usage

index_jackknife(idx, source_col, key_cols, time_col, weights, ...)

Arguments

idx, source_col, key_cols, time_col, weights

As in aggregate_index().

...

Further arguments passed to aggregate_index() (index_col, type, cap), used both for the full index and for every leave-one-out index: with type = "arithmetic" the range refers to arithmetic aggregates.

Value

A data.table with columns key_cols, time_col, the full index (index_col), n_sources, jk_min, jk_max (range of the leave-one-out indices), jk_source (source whose removal moves the index most) and jk_shift (leave-one-out index minus full index for that source).

Details

Without cap, the full weighted mean (of logs for type = "geometric", of indices for "arithmetic") is a convex combination of the leave-one-out means, so the full index always lies in [jk_min, jk_max]. In cells where a single source is present, removing it leaves no index; such leave-one-out values are ignored.

Examples

weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2024-01-01") + 7L * (0:3)
idx <- data.table::data.table(
  source = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 4), week = rep(weeks, 3),
  indice = c(100, 101, 102, 103, 100, 99, 98, 97, 100, 100, 101, 101)
)
w <- data.table::data.table(source = c("a", "b", "c"), w = c(3, 1, 1))
index_jackknife(idx, "source", NULL, "week", w)
#>          week   indice n_sources    jk_min   jk_max jk_source   jk_shift
#>        <IDat>    <num>     <int>     <num>    <num>    <char>      <num>
#> 1: 2024-01-01 100.0000         3 100.00000 100.0000         a  0.0000000
#> 2: 2024-01-08 100.3968         3  99.49874 100.7491         a -0.8980546
#> 3: 2024-01-15 100.9880         3  99.48869 101.7491         a -1.4992657
#> 4: 2024-01-22 101.3727         3  98.97980 102.4963         a -2.3928907
